title: Blink: External LED
description: Blink an LED wired to a breadboard through a 220 ohm current-limiting resistor, switched on and off from pin 13.

steps.clip: Grab an Arduino Uno, a breadboard, a 220 ohm resistor, an LED, and two jumper wires.
Push the resistor's two legs into two neighboring columns on the breadboard.
hints: Either leg can go in either hole — this resistor works the same either way round.
Use two columns right next to each other, both below the center gap.

steps.clip: Connect an orange wire from pin 13 to one leg of the resistor.
hints: Either leg of the resistor works for this wire.
This wire carries the on/off signal from pin 13.

steps.clip: Push the LED into the breadboard so its long leg (anode) shares a column with the resistor's free leg, and its short leg (cathode) sits in a fresh column.
hints: The long leg is the anode — it goes toward the resistor.
The short leg is the cathode — give it its own empty column; it lights only this way round.

steps.clip: Run a black wire from the LED's short leg to a GND pin on the Uno.
hints: Use the GND pin right next to pin 13.

steps.clip: Upload the sketch and watch the LED blink once a second.
